findings.title: $__range variable queries will now be incorrectly split
findings.body: The new code interpolates queries via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before the `querySupportsSplitting` check is evaluated. The existing check at line 287 (`!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)`) is supposed to prevent queries containing `$__range` from being split, with a comment explaining that otherwise the interpolated `$__range` value is wrong because it gets interpolated against the split (sub-request) time range. After this change the interpolation runs first on the original full range, so `$__range` is already replaced with a literal value (e.g. `2d`) by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable` is consulted, and the function returns `false`. As a result, queries that were previously excluded from splitting will now be split, and each sub-request will receive the same `$__range` value computed from the full time range instead of the per-chunk range. The corresponding code path is hit by `runSplitQuery` and by `runShardSplitQuery` (which calls `runSplitQuery` for each shard group), so this affects both splitting modes. The PR adds no test for a `$__range` expression to guard this behavior.

findings.title: Stale comment about $__range interpolation
findings.body: The comment in `querySupportsSplitting` states that `$__range` 'is interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange'. After this PR, interpolation is performed on the frontend inside `runSplitQuery` (and inside `runShardSplitQuery`) before the split happens, using the full time range from `request.range`. The comment is now misleading and contradicts the new behavior; it should be updated to describe the new interpolation point and the implication for `$__range` queries.

findings.title: No test covers the $__range case after the interpolation change
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only exercises `$__auto` and `$step` and uses a `replace` mock that does not touch `$__range`. There is also no existing test in either `querySplitting.test.ts` or `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` that asserts what happens to a query containing `$__range` when it goes through `runSplitQuery` or `runShardSplitQuery`. Given that the change moves interpolation ahead of the `querySupportsSplitting` check, a regression test using `$__range` (or `__range`, `${__range}`) is needed to ensure the existing 'do not split range-variable queries' invariant still holds.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in the sharded path
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` for every target on line 52, and then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` forwards those (already-interpolated) targets into `runSplitQuery`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again for each target of every sub-request (line 299 of `querySplitting.ts`). The shard test was updated to assert this redundancy: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single-target request that issues 4 sub-requests. Beyond the wasted work, the second interpolation runs over expressions that have already been mutated to add `__stream_shard__` selectors; if any of those new literal substrings happen to collide with template-variable syntax used by the templateSrv, the result is non-obvious. Either `runShardSplitQuery` should pass already-interpolated targets through and skip the re-interpolation in `runSplitQuery`, or the interpolation should be done only inside `runSplitQuery` as before.

findings.title: New interpolation test reuses the outer `datasource` variable but bypasses beforeEach mocks
findings.body: The 'Interpolates queries before execution' test reassigns `datasource` after the `beforeEach` has already installed `applyTemplateVariables` and `languageProvider.fetchLabelValues` mocks. The new datasource is created with a custom `replace` function and is intended to exercise the real `applyTemplateVariables`, but the previous test file conventions (see 'Interpolates queries before running' at line 110) explicitly mock `applyTemplateVariables` to control interpolation. Mixing the two approaches in the same `describe` block means the behavior under test is not really 'does querySplitting interpolate before execution?' but 'does it call applyTemplateVariables that happens to interpolate via this replace function?'. The test is also fragile to any future change in the real `applyTemplateVariables` (e.g. handling of `$__range`) because it does not stub it explicitly. Consider mocking `applyTemplateVariables` here too, or moving this case to a dedicated test that documents the use of the real implementation.
